Re:

Compliance Filing of PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. in Response to Order on 
Rehearing, Clarification, Compliance Filing, and Paper Hearing in Docket 
Nos. EL25-49-002, et al. 
 
Dear Secretary Reese: 
Pursuant to section 206 of the Federal Power Act,1 PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. 
(“PJM”) hereby submits proposed revisions to the PJM Open Access Transmission Tariff 
(“Tariff”)2 in accordance with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s 
(“Commission”) directives in its June 18, 2026, Order on Rehearing, Clarification, 
Compliance Filing, and Paper Hearing (“June Order”) 3 in Docket No. EL25-49-002, et al.4  
As discussed below, PJM proposes an effective date for the Tariff revisions in Parts I, III,

Transmission Tariff (“Tariff”) or the Amended and Restated Operating Agreement of PJM Interconnection, 
L.L.C.  
3 PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., 195 FERC ¶ 61,209 (2026).

Commission’s Large Load Order (as defined below) invites.  PJM is identifying, with stakeholder 
engagement, what changes to its Tariff may be needed on a holistic basis to develop a Federal Power Act 
section 205 filing to fully respond to the Large Load Order.  PJM intends to submit that filing by mid-
November 2026.  Today’s partial compliance filing should not be construed to, and is in no way intended to, 
limit the reforms PJM will pursue to meet the challenges of the moment and resolve the Commission’s 
preliminary findings in the Large Load Order.

To improve clarity and consistency in the Tariff and make the Tariff easier to 
understand, PJM also proposes minor revisions to Parts I, III, VI, VII, VIII, IX and X to 
cross-reference Part VIII as needed; make clear that the Provisional Interconnection 
Service and Necessary Study process provided in Part VIII is available to Interconnection 
Customers under Part VI, as well as to Expedited Interconnection Track Project Developers 
under Part X; applies to those entities and to Eligible Customers under Part III; and clarify 
that the use of the terms “Project Developer,” “Generation Project Developer,” and 
“Generation Interconnection Agreement” under Tariff, Part VIII shall be understood to 
reference Interconnection Customers and Interconnection Service Agreements (“ISA”) 
under Part VI, as appropriate. 
 
INTRODUCTION  
A. 
Commission December Order 
On December 18, 2025, the Commission issued the Order on Show Cause 
(“December Order”) finding the Tariff unjust and unreasonable due to the lack of

PJM to make a number of compliance and informational filings.12   
First, the December Order directed PJM to make a compliance filing within 30 days 
to clarify the rates, terms, and conditions that apply to an Interconnection Customer13 
seeking to serve Co-Located Load with new generation, including with Surplus 
Interconnection Service and Provisional Interconnection Service.14 
Second, the December Order directed PJM to make a compliance filing within 60 days 
to, inter alia, modify the Retail BTMG netting rules to limit netting over a certain 
threshold;15 add certain requirements for Eligible Customers taking transmission service 
on behalf of Co-Located Loads;16 and clarify that existing customers seeking to modify 
ISAs/GIAs to accommodate Generating Facilities serving Co-Located Load must follow 
Necessary Study processes.17    
Third, the December Order ordered a paper hearing to determine the appropriate rates, 
terms, and conditions for the three new transmission service.18  Among other things, the 
Commission asked PJM to address (1) the appropriate rates, terms and conditions for the 
new services; (2) the appropriate rates for customers taking new transmission services for

Co-Located Load; and (7) appropriate procedures for curtailment and load shed.19 
B. 
PJM Compliance Filings 
1. 
Thirty-Day Compliance Filing 
On January 20, 2026, PJM made its 30-day compliance filing in Docket No. ER26-
1088-000 pursuant to the December Order (“Thirty-Day Compliance Filing”).20  The 
Thirty-Day Compliance Filing proposed to clarify certain aspects of the Tariff for those 
seeking to serve Co-Located Load with new Generating Facilities.21  Among other changes, 
the Thirty-Day Compliance Filing proposed to clarify that existing services in the Tariff 
could be used to serve Project Developers serving Co-Located Load, including Provisional 
Interconnection Service and Surplus Interconnection Service.22  The Thirty-Day 
Compliance Filing also clarified the ability of Project Developers serving Co-Located Load 
to request interconnection service below nameplate capacity and the potential to accelerate 
the interconnection process under certain circumstances.23

On April 16, 2026, the Commission accepted in part and rejected in part PJM’s 
compliance filing.24  The Commission rejected PJM’s revisions to the proposed definition 
of Co-Located Load because PJM’s proposal to deviate from this definition by replacing 
the term “Point of Interconnection” with “Point of Change in Ownership” did not provide 
sufficient explanation as to how this proposed deviation complies with the Commission’s 
directive in the December Order.25  The Commission also rejected proposed Tariff 
revisions relating to BTMG as constituting changes that were outside the scope of the 
original proceeding, and directed PJM to remove revisions that incorporated the term Co-
Located Load into Tariff sections related to BTMG Application Requirements.26  On 
May 18, 2026, PJM submitted a compliance filing to comply with the directives set forth 
in the April 16 Order.27 
2. 
Sixty-Day Compliance Filing 
On February 23, 2026, PJM submitted its 60-day compliance filing in response to 
the December Order (“Sixty-Day Compliance Filing”).28  The Sixty-Day Compliance 
Filing proposed Tariff revisions to:  (1) revise its BTMG Tariff provisions; (2) establish 
three new transmission services for Eligible Customers seeking to take service on behalf 
of Co-Located Load; and (3) revise its necessary studies processes, among other changes.29

proposed new transmission services changes.31 
3. 
Paper hearing on new transmission services 
PJM submitted its initial brief in Docket Nos. EL25-49-000 and EL25-49-001 to 
address the Commission’s finding in the December Order that additional record evidence 
was needed to set the appropriate replacement rates, terms, and conditions for new 
transmission services for Eligible Customers serving Co-Located Load, including for 
Interim NITS, Firm Contract Demand Transmission Service, and Non-Firm Contract 
Demand Transmission Service.32  PJM’s initial brief set forth the non-rate terms and 
conditions for these new transmission services along with illustrative Tariff language.  
Various parties protested aspects of PJM’s illustrative Tariff language.33  In its reply brief, 
PJM proposed certain refinements to the illustrative language.34

C. 
The Commission’s June Order 
On June 18, 2026, the Commission issued the June Order, addressing the Sixty-
Day Compliance Filing, the paper hearing submissions, and requests for rehearing and 
clarification of the December Order.35  
The June Order found that PJM’s Sixty-Day Compliance Filing partially complies 
with the directives of the December Order, and the Commission accepted in part and 
rejected in part PJM’s proposed Tariff revisions and ordered PJM to submit a further 
compliance filing within 60 days.36  Additionally, the June Order found that in response to 
the record developed in the paper hearing, certain rates, terms, and conditions for the new 
transmission services as directed in the December Order (i.e., Interim NITS, Firm Contract 
Demand transmission service, and Non-Firm Contract Demand transmission service) are 
just and reasonable and directed PJM to make a compliance filing to revise its Tariff.37  
D. 
Large Load Order 
The same day it issued the June Order, the Commission also issued a new show 
cause order to PJM concerning Large Loads (“Large Load Order”).38  The Large Load 
Order found that several aspects of PJM’s Tariff appeared unjust and unreasonable due to 
the lack of specific procedures for integrating large loads, including a lack of procedures 
for interconnection studies, processing transmission service requests, and constructing 
network upgrades without cost shifting.39  The Large Load Order also found PJM’s Tariff

appeared to be unjust and unreasonable due to a lack of transmission service options for 
customers serving large loads that are willing and able to limit their withdrawals from the 
Transmission System.40  The Large Load Order further found that PJM’s Tariff appeared 
to be unjust and unreasonable due to a lack of mechanisms to ensure that costs are not 
shifted between transmission customers.41 
To address these issues, the Large Load Order directed PJM to make two 
compliance filings.42  First, the Large Load Order directed PJM to submit an informational 
filing within 30 days to explain how PJM intends to ensure that it has adequate generation 
to serve existing and new large loads.43  Second, the Large Load Order directed PJM to 
submit within 60 days a compliance filing to explain whether its Tariff remains just and 
reasonable in light of the issues identified in the order, or to propose Tariff changes that 
would remedy the identified concerns.44  The Commission noted that it would entertain 
requests to hold the show cause proceedings in abeyance if PJM demonstrated a plan to 
file changes pursuant to Federal Power Act section 205 to address the identified concerns.45 
E. 
Partial Extension 
On July 28, 2026, PJM filed a motion for extension of time to meet certain 
compliance requirements in the June Order.46  PJM explained that due to the significant

The Commission issued a notice on August 14, 2026 granting PJM’s requested 
extension and abeyance.52  This filing represents PJM’s partial compliance filing with the 
June Order, as outlined in the July 28, 2026 motion for extension of time. 
 
DESCRIPTION OF CHANGES  
A. 
Prohibition on Serving Co-Located Load from Existing Generators

will prohibit Interconnection Customers from serving Co-Located Loads from new and

implementing any planned modifications to its facilities until the Necessary Studies are

and (3) not begin serving Eligible Load until the entire scope of the work under their GIA 
as amended after the Necessary Study process is complete.  These combined revisions

B. 
Revisions to Retail Behind the Meter Generation Definition 
In the Sixty-Day Compliance Filing, PJM had proposed to define Retail BTMG as 
load being served by a generation facility with a nameplate capacity of 50 MW or less.57  
PJM also proposed to implement various exemptions from the netting limit for a transition 
period, contractual rights, and qualifying facilities under Public Utility Regulatory Policies 
Act via the Retail BTMG definition.58  The June Order, however, rejected PJM’s proposed 
50 MW limit and instead directed PJM to permit Retail BTMG netting up to a 50 MW 
materiality threshold.59  Consistent with the extension motion, PJM is continuing to work 
with stakeholders to develop Tariff language to implement the 50 MW netting provisions 
for Retail BTMG.  However, for purposes of allowing Eligible Customers with load served 
by Retail BTMG to take Interim NITS,60 PJM is proposing a revised definition of Retail

C. 
Expansion of Service to “Eligible Load” for Load with BTMG 
The June Order directed PJM to expand the availability of the December Order’s 
new transmission services to Network Customers serving load with BTMG that are willing 
and able to limit their withdrawals from the Transmission System under certain 
circumstances.62  The Commission directed PJM to either add a definition of “Eligible 
Load” or propose other changes to implement this directive.63  Consistent with this 
directive, PJM is proposing to add the term Eligible Load to the Tariff to encompass both 
Co-Located Load and Load with BTMG.64  To that end, PJM is proposing to add to the 
Tariff, Part I, section 1, Definitions the term “Eligible Load” defined as “Co-Located Load 
or load connected to Behind the Meter Generation.”65  Further consistent with the 
Commission’s directive to propose other Tariff changes necessary to expand the 
availability of these new services, PJM is proposing to add to the term “Eligible Generating 
Facility” to the Tariff to encompass both a Co-Located Generating Facility or Retail 
BTMG.66  In addition, PJM is proposing conforming changes to replace “Co-Located

D. 
Elimination of New GIA Requirement 
PJM previously proposed to require all Eligible Customers that intend to serve Co-

EFFECTIVE DATE AND WAIVER REQUEST 
In accordance with the Commission’s regulations,132 PJM requests an effective date 
for the compliance changes in Parts I, III, VI, VII, VIII, and IX of the Tariff of 
October 17, 2026, which is 61 days after the date of this filing.   
Consistent with the Commission’s directive to consider whether Interim NITS 
could be implemented earlier than originally proposed,133 PJM is proposing an effective 
date of July 1, 2028, for the new Part XI regarding the provision of Interim NITS.  At 
present, PJM can provide partial NITS, i.e., NITS in an amount less than requested and/or 
for a term shorter than requested, to Co-Located Load through the Necessary Study process 
and therefore is proposing an October 17, 2026 effective date for the bulk of the revisions 
proposed in this filing.  However, PJM Operations personnel will need to implement 
additional tools and processes before they will be able to monitor and curtail, as needed, 
the new non-firm Interim NITS product proposed in Tariff, Part XI.  PJM anticipates it will 
be able to develop, procure, and implement those tools and processes by mid-2028, and
